page: Microsoft Azure FX64-16ms_v2 is a memory-intensive virtual machine instance belonging to the FXmsv2 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor with a base clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The instance is configured with 16 dedicated vCPUs derived from 8 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. A key hardware characteristic is its massive memory capacity of 1344.0 GB, yielding an exceptionally high resource density of 84.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, though it is premium storage capable.

In benchmark evaluations, the processor demonstrates strong single-core capabilities, achieving a Geekbench single-core score of 2364.0 and a text processing score of 2950.0, both placing in the top tier. Multi-core performance is moderate, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 13643.0 and a stress-ng multi-core score of 17775.0. Memory performance is highlighted by a strong write bandwidth of 91.25 GB/sec for large uncached blocks, while read bandwidth for large blocks sits at an average of 131.84 GB/sec. Single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression also register in the top 25% tier, processing at 34.83 GB/sec and 14.28 GB/sec respectively.

The primary tradeoff of the FX64-16ms_v2 is the absence of local storage, requiring external premium storage attachments for persistent data. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the instance offers high memory density relative to its compute footprint, making it a specialized option for workloads where memory capacity is the primary bottleneck rather than parallel CPU scaling. It is suited for large in-memory databases, memory-intensive data processing, caching layers such as Redis, and enterprise applications requiring massive RAM allocations without the overhead of high vCPU counts.
